Vasa deferentia Each spermiducal funnel posteriorly leads into a slender and internally ciliated thread like structure called sperm duct or vas deferens. Two vasa deferentia of same side run downward very closely on the either side of nerve cord along the ventral body wall. They reach up to the 18th segment and join with the prostatic duct. 6. Prostate glands They are a pair of dirty white coloured, flat, solid, irregular shaped and lobulated structures on either side of the alimentary canal extending from about 16th to 21st segment. Each gland consists of mainly two parts: a big glandular part with many lobules and a small non-glandular part composed of many small ductules. Small ductules get united together and finally form prostatic duct. A prostatic duct and two vasa deferentia of same side remain separated inside a muscular sheath, forming a single tube which emerges out from prostate gland. The single tube that emerges out of each prostate gland is called common prostatic and spermatic duct. Common prostatic and spermatic duct of either side, after emergence, gets curved down and opens exteriorly by male genital opening in 18th segment. Prostate glands secrete prostatic fluid of unknown function. 7. Accessory glands Accessory glands are rounded white masses which are altogether 2 pair in number, each pair situated in 17th and 19th segment, one on either side of nerve cord. These glands open outside ventrally by minute ducts on the two pair of genital papillae. The secretion of accessory glands helps to unite worms during copulation. B. Female reproductive organs 1. Ovaries In the 13th segment, there is a pair of small, white, lobulated ovaries hanging down from the intersegmental septum of 12th and 13th segment, each on the either side of ventral nerve cord. Each ovary is a compact structure with finger like processes in which ova of various stages are found in linear sequence. Larger sized or mature ova are found at the distal part whereas immature ones at the proximal part.
